subject: Agreement packaging: privacy alignment & cross-border safeguards
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena@brightpath.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@brightpath.com
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Pre-execution: clause preferences and SCCs

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the productive demo last week — BrightPath is excited to move toward contracting. Before our procurement team kicks the PO over, legal asked for a quick summary of Redwood's preferred approach to cross-border safeguards for this engagement. The main items they flagged:

- Which SCCs you intend to flow (controller->processor vs processor->processor) and whether you prefer to include them as an exhibit or a separate annex.
- Whether Redwood will accept a limited subprocessor delegation clause or require advance approval for certain categories.
- Any planned transfer impact addendum or mitigation language (we're in the EU and have some sensitive client data).

I've attached our latest Order Form (v3) with a few internal comments; procurement would like to keep the signature window to two weeks if possible. Can you confirm the right point people on your side for the legal redline and an expected timeline to resolution?

Best,

Elena Rossi
Senior Contracts Manager
BrightPath Systems
Attachments: BrightPath_OrderForm_v3_redlines.docx
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@brightpath.com>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 11:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Pre-execution: clause preferences and SCCs

Hi Elena — thanks for the note and the Order Form. Looping in Jonas (legal lead) and Ben (revenue/ops) so we can coordinate.

Quick answers up front:
- SCCs / transfer mechanism: Redwood's standard is to include the EU SCCs as an exhibit to the MSA and reference them from the Order Form. That keeps the Order Form clean and allows us to swap approved SCC versions without touching commercial language.
- Subprocessors: we typically allow delegation to named subprocessors with a simple notice clause; for categories we consider high-risk (e.g., sensitive PHI processing or managed hosting in new jurisdictions) we are open to a narrow approval right.
- Transfer impact addendum: for customers with heightened concerns (healthcare, regulated finance) we propose a short Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA) that documents mitigations (KMS regioning, contract limits, logging/audit evidence).

Jonas — can your team take the BrightPath redlines and produce a single-markup MSA + DPA exhibit that we can send back? Procurement asked for a 10 business day turnaround from receipt of our redline. If that's optimistic, flag the expected timeline.

Ben — please confirm if two-week signature window is achievable from a commercial perspective or whether we should flag a potential one-week extension to procurement.

Thanks,

Laura Bennett
Head of Legal Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Elena Rossi <elena@brightpath.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Pre-execution: clause preferences and SCCs

Thanks — reviewed the Order Form comments. High-level plan below and attachments with proposed artifacts: SCCs-comparison-table.xlsx (shows mapping to our template), DPA-proposed-exhibit.pdf (clean exhibit to attach to MSA).

Action items / timeline:
1) I'll produce a combined MSA + DPA markup (tracked changes) by Tue 24 Nov (5 business days). That will:
   - Insert the SCCs as Exhibit B and cross-reference in Order Form section 9.
   - Add a short Transfer Impact Addendum framework with optional mitigations customers can select.
2) For subprocessor approvals: propose a two-track approach — (a) standard notice for routine cloud infra subprocessors, (b) explicit consent for the small list of high-risk categories. We'll flag the categories in the DPA exhibit.
3) Ben: can you confirm if we can accept a two-week signature target conditional on the DPA exhibit being in place, or do you want procurement to expect staggered signoff (commercial first, DPA TIA within 10 business days)?

Notes on evidence: BrightPath asked about evidence for KMS regioning and logging/audit. Our standard evidence package is: SOC 2 summary + KMS architecture diagram + export controls statement. If BrightPath needs specific artifacts we should schedule a short evidence call with our security team.

Attachments: SCCs-comparison-table.xlsx, DPA-proposed-exhibit.pdf

--
Jonas Weber
VP, Contracts & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Elena Rossi <elena@brightpath.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 14:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Pre-execution: clause preferences and SCCs

All — thanks. Two confirmatory notes:

1) Two-week signature window is fine from sales ops if the Order Form commercial terms don't change. If substantial commercial redlines occur, procurement may pause; we'll call that out.
2) We prefer to return the commercial MSA + Order Form with the DPA exhibit included as a single packet. If BrightPath needs faster execution, we can do staged signoff (commercial now, DPA TIA executed within 10 business days).

I'll set up a 30-minute call for Mon 23 Nov at 09:00 CET to walk through outstanding items and agree a final turn. Laura/Jonas — would you be available for that slot? Elena — if that works for you I'll send an invite and include a brief agenda.

Thanks,

Ben Carter
Senior Manager, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
Attachments referenced: BrightPath_OrderForm_v3_redlines.docx, SCCs-comparison-table.xlsx, DPA-proposed-exhibit.pdf
